text:
Sanjay: Heads up - following the quant profiles RFC, I ran into a shipping edge where models with post-load requantization fail kernel selection because the loader flips the dtype after the runtime has already picked kernels. Need a short follow-up on the loader/runtime handshake.
Maya: ugh, saw that in a canary too. Are we talking per-layer requantize-on-load or a global rewrite?
Sanjay: Per-model manifest opt-in. Some customers want aggressive i8->4bit recompute to save memory, but it changes operator footprints.
Jordan: The core issue is ordering: loader should expose a promised runtime shape + bitwidth surface before runtime binds kernels. We can add a 2-phase bind: declare -> negotiate -> bind.
Maya: negotiate how? do we need RTT for each model load? that's expensive on startup.
Jordan: Not per-request. One-shot at load. Proposal: model manifest contains a small "quant_handshake" header that lists allowed fallbacks and max async warmup time. Runtime reads header and reserves kernel set. If loader changes bitwidth later it must call runtime.rebind().
Sanjay: That sounds reasonable. Example manifest snippet I sketched:
```json
{"quant_handshake": {"allowed_bitwidths": ["fp8","int8","4bit"], "default_profile": "int8_safety", "requant_on_load": {"enabled": true, "strategy": "per_layer", "max_layers_requant": 16}, "fallback_policy": "int8->fp16", "hysteresis_ms": 200}}
```
Maya: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) who owns rebind latency budget (loader or runtime)? 2) how do we signal failure so shady models don't bork the serving process?
Jordan: 1) loader opts into a max_rebind_latency in the header; runtime can decline if it breaks SLOs. 2) for failure we return a structured error with code QUANT_BIND_FAIL and either a suggested fallback profile or a guidance to fall through to hosted fallback.
Sanjay: Example error payload (idea):
```json
{"error":"QUANT_BIND_FAIL","message":"requested 4bit per-layer requantization not supported on this device kernel set","suggested_profiles":["int8_safety","fp8_mixed"]}
```
Maya: We also need observability hooks: tag model loads with quant_profile and emit quant_bind_time, kernels_selected, and fallback_triggered boolean. Ops need to correlate with degradation SLI.
Jordan: Agreed. Also add a compat-check flag: runtime.can_support_profile(manifest_quant_header) that returns quick boolean without binding, used in preflight.
RuntimeBot: deploy-bot posted: "canary: runtime-v2.3.1 with handshake proto + loader patch deployed to canary cluster" :rocket:
Sanjay: Ok next steps: Jordan to draft handshake proto + loader API, Maya to update ops telemetry spec, I will add RFC appendix for rebind semantics. Target: canary by next Tue.
Maya: +1, i'll flag on SLO board and add alert if quant_bind_time > 500ms during warmup. :thumbsup:
Jordan: i'll sketch code stub in the repo and ping during PR.
Sanjay: thanks, closing thread.
